title: Automation Framework Standard
content: All automation frameworks must support reusable architecture, logging, exception handling, modular design, retry mechanism, maintainable structure, reusable utilities, reporting integration, environment configuration management, and separation of test logic from utility logic. Frameworks must avoid duplicated code and hardcoded test data.

title: Test Case Writing Standard
content: Every test case must contain testcase id, title, business objective, preconditions, test steps, expected results, validation points, negative scenarios, priority, test data, dependency information, cleanup steps, and execution type. Test cases must be readable and traceable to Jira requirements.

title: Coding Standard
content: Code must follow clean naming conventions, reusable design, modular implementation, proper logging, exception handling, and avoid duplicated logic. Methods should remain small and maintain single responsibility. Hardcoded credentials, URLs, and test data are prohibited.

title: Wait Strategy
content: Selenium automation must always use explicit waits using WebDriverWait. Avoid time.sleep() and unnecessary implicit waits. Synchronization should be implemented using visibility, clickability, presence, or invisibility conditions depending on UI behavior.

title: Locator Strategy
content: Locator priority should follow ID, NAME, CSS Selector, then XPath. Dynamic XPath should be avoided unless no alternative exists. Centralize locators using Page Object Model. Avoid absolute XPath and unstable DOM references.

title: Framework Design
content: Selenium framework must follow Page Object Model architecture with separation between pages, tests, utilities, configuration, reports, and test data. Framework should support reusable wrappers, retry logic, screenshots on failure, and parallel execution.

title: Test Stability Rules
content: Automation scripts must avoid flaky behavior by using synchronization, stable locators, retry logic, and proper cleanup. Shared state between tests should be avoided. Tests must support isolated execution.

title: Assertion Standard
content: All Selenium tests must contain validations and assertions for business outcomes. Assertions must validate UI state, messages, API responses, database updates, or workflow completion. Scripts without assertions are invalid.

title: UFT Standard
content: UFT automation must use reusable actions, shared object repositories, reusable VBScript libraries, recovery scenarios, synchronization points, and descriptive programming standards where applicable. Framework should minimize duplicated logic.

title: Object Repository Policy
content: Shared object repositories must follow consistent naming conventions, avoid duplicate objects, support maintainability, and organize objects logically based on modules and workflows.

title: Recovery Scenario Standard
content: Recovery scenarios must handle unexpected popups, browser crashes, session timeouts, and synchronization failures. Recovery logic should avoid stopping entire execution suites whenever possible.

title: PR Validation
content: Pull requests must follow coding standards, naming conventions, modular design, reusable architecture, logging standards, exception handling, and framework guidelines. PRs must avoid hardcoded waits, duplicated logic, unstable locators, and unnecessary complexity.

title: Security Validation
content: PRs must not contain hardcoded passwords, tokens, API keys, production URLs, customer information, or sensitive business data. Security-sensitive values must use environment variables or secured configuration files.

title: Code Quality Review
content: PR review must validate maintainability, readability, modularity, reusable methods, assertion quality, synchronization strategy, reporting implementation, logging coverage, and test stability. Large methods and duplicated logic should be flagged.

title: Story Validation
content: Every Jira user story must contain business objective, functional requirement, acceptance criteria, validation conditions, dependency details, impacted modules, negative scenarios, and API/UI impact details. Missing details should be flagged during analysis.

title: Requirement Gap Analysis
content: AI validation must identify incomplete acceptance criteria, unclear business flows, missing validations, missing negative scenarios, missing dependency information, and inconsistent workflow descriptions. Suggested improvements should be generated automatically.

title: Acceptance Criteria Rules
content: Acceptance criteria must be testable, measurable, unambiguous, and aligned with business outcomes. Each criterion should support positive and negative validation scenarios.

title: API Validation
content: API automation must validate status codes, response schema, response payload, headers, authorization, response time, negative scenarios, invalid payload handling, retry behavior, and error messages.

title: API Security Rules
content: API testing must validate authentication, authorization, token expiry, invalid access handling, role-based access, data masking, and secure transport validation where applicable.

title: Response Validation Standard
content: Response validation must compare expected schema, field types, mandatory fields, null handling, error codes, and business response values. Unexpected fields or missing fields should be flagged.

title: Regression Suite Standard
content: Regression suites must prioritize business-critical workflows, reusable validations, stable automation coverage, and execution reliability. Failed scripts should include detailed logging and screenshots.

title: Smoke Suite Standard
content: Smoke suites must validate application availability, login functionality, major business workflows, API availability, environment stability, and critical navigation paths before full execution.

title: Banking Validation Rules
content: Banking validations must include mandatory KYC checks, transaction validation, authorization validation, account state validation, balance validation, session timeout handling, and audit logging verification.

title: Payment Workflow Validation
content: Payment workflows must validate successful transaction flow, insufficient balance handling, duplicate transaction prevention, retry handling, timeout scenarios, authorization failures, and reconciliation status validation.

title: MCP Integration Standard
content: MCP is responsible for live access to Jira, Confluence, Git repositories, filesystem access, PR data, assigned ticket dashboards, and historical automation lookup. MCP should not permanently store transient execution data inside ChromaDB.

title: RAG Knowledge Policy
content: ChromaDB stores reusable organizational knowledge including SOPs, coding policies, testing standards, framework rules, PR review standards, domain validations, reusable automation patterns, and historical approved examples.

title: Approved Automation Pattern
content: Approved automation scripts should demonstrate reusable design, explicit waits, assertion coverage, modular architecture, proper reporting, stable locators, logging integration, and maintainable structure.

title: Automation Anti Pattern
content: Avoid hardcoded waits, duplicated locators, duplicated business logic, shared test dependencies, unstable XPath usage, large monolithic scripts, missing assertions, and direct production environment modifications.
